root_cause_label: Final Implementation Omits is_active/active->status Mapping and index=False; Preceded by Extended PYTHONPATH Environment Battle
one_sentence_failure_summary: After spending most of the trajectory fighting a harness PYTHONPATH conflict that shadowed the real pandas with a stub module, the agent produced a final implementation that omits the is_active/active-to-status field mapping for source_b and source_c, excludes status from conflict detection, and calls to_parquet() without index=False.
t_err_evidence: In step 25 the agent writes the final implementation: map_b only renames user_id/name/email_address/created_at but never maps is_active->status; map_c only renames userId/userName/joined but never maps active->status; the conflict loop only checks ['name','email','created_date'] and omits 'status'; merged.to_parquet(output_parquet) has no index=False, so user_id stays as the index rather than a column.
t_commit_evidence: After writing the script in step 25 the agent immediately executes it in step 26 and claims success; no further edits are made, so the flawed implementation is locked in at step 25.
trigger_explanation: The task spec explicitly requires mapping is_active (source_b) and active (source_c) to a unified 'status' field and normalizing them to 'active'/'inactive' strings, and detecting status conflicts. The agent observed is_active in source_b's header at step 3 but never connected it to the output schema requirement; the final script silently drops these fields and ignores status conflicts entirely.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 7-20 show repeated execution failures (ImportError for pyarrow, then AttributeError 'module pandas has no attribute read_json') across multiple retries; the agent repeatedly reinstalls packages and manipulates sys.path without resolving the underlying PYTHONPATH conflict until step 21.
